en: The publication path (<t1/>, modelled in <t2/>) does not regenerate: the committed projections are already checked, so publishing renders them. Three facts are kept separate because they fail separately: the build succeeded, the deployment was pushed, and the public site serves the new commit. Only the last is verified against the public endpoint — <t3/> on <t4/> carries the commit it was built from. In the deploy job that verification (<t5/>) is advisory: the step may fail without failing the job, and the job reports "pushed" and "serving" as separate facts. What judges is the <t6/> gate, run at finish, which checks that the served commit is on master and that no publication has been owed longer than the deploy window (<t7/>).
cs: Publikační cesta (<t1/>, modelovaná v <t2/>) nic nepřegenerovává: commitnuté projekce jsou už zkontrolovány, takže publikace je vykresluje. Jen poslední se ověřuje proti veřejnému endpointu — <t3/> na <t4/> nese commit, ze kterého byl postaven. V jobu nasazení je toto ověření (<t5/>) poradní: krok může selhat, aniž by selhal job, a job hlásí „pushed“ a „serving“ jako samostatné fakty. Rozhoduje kontrola <t6/>, spouštěná při finish, která ověřuje, že servírovaný commit je na masteru a že žádná publikace není dlužna déle než okno nasazení (<t7/>).

en: <t1>Every Majordomus server is a rendezvous.</t1> <t2/> accepts a signed envelope, verifies it exactly as a datagram, and answers with the envelopes it holds — each verifiable end-to-end on its own signature, so a poisoned rendezvous can withhold nodes but cannot invent one. The "mothership" is any node the declaration points at; the local registry stays the only truth, and a rendezvous failure stretches a backoff and stops nothing else.
